name: Question 6
problem: Which of the following matrices has a rank of $3?$
worked_solution:
First, notice that a matrix of rank $3$ must have at least $3$ columns and at least $3$ rows. 
So, we disregard the following matrices:

- $A$ since it has only $2$ rows.

- $B$ since it has only $2$ rows (and only $2$ columns).

- $E$ since it has only $2$ columns.

Also, the matrix must have $3$ pivot columns. As we can see, the matrix $C$ has exactly $3$ pivot columns, while the matrix $D$ has only $2$ pivot columns. So, $\text{rank}(C)=3$ and $\text{rank}(D)=2.$

Therefore, the correct answer is the matrix $C.$

Question 6
?

Which of the following matrices has a rank of 3?

a
A=[210100−1000]
b
E=[−12010000]
c
C=[213100−10210000200000]
d
B=[5−103]
e
D=[3210−12000000]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that a matrix of rank 3 must have at least 3 columns and at least 3 rows. So, we disregard the following matrices:

  • A since it has only 2 rows.

  • B since it has only 2 rows (and only 2 columns).

  • E since it has only 2 columns.

Also, the matrix must have 3 pivot columns. As we can see, the matrix C has exactly 3 pivot columns, while the matrix D has only 2 pivot columns. So, rank(C)=3 and rank(D)=2.

Therefore, the correct answer is the matrix C.
